label: input b at position 0 or 1 of the original sequence
explanation: A token-and-position feature: fires only when the input token is b at step 0 or 1 of the original phase. Every activation has in_tok = b. Strongest at t=0 (always hits the max value of 3.655, about 64% of activation mass). At t=1 it fires at about 0.5-0.6 of max, with the exact size depending on the token before it (e.g. after d about 0.62, after o/r about 0.53). Rarely fires weakly on b at t=2 (about 600 steps, mostly when the sequence starts with d) and almost never later. Does not fire on b anywhere later in the original phase, at the delimiter, or during the copy phase, and never on any other token.

issues: Claims hold up. Every activation has in_tok=b (33918/33918 on dev). The feature is silent at the delimiter. Copy-phase firing is near zero: 24 steps out of 90984 copy-phase b steps, mass about 0. Test split with the original predicate gives precision 1.0, recall 0.980, F1 0.990 and 0 false positives.
Mass split matches: t=0 holds 0.643 of activation mass, t=1 0.356, t=2 0.002. Firing at t>=3 is about 24 steps.

One small systematic miss class: b at t=2 when orig(0)=d. It fires about 96% of the time there (precision 0.961, 537 predicted). These are weak activations (about 0.04-0.15 of max) and hold only about 0.2% of mass. The explanation already mentions this ('mostly in sequences starting with d'). The one exception is sequences starting 'd j b', which do not fire.
Adding that clause, (in_tok==b) & ((t<=1) | ((t==2) & (orig(0)==d))), raises test F1 from 0.990 to 0.998. That is too small a gain to call the label wrong.
Not checked: the claimed t=1 magnitudes depending on the previous token (0.62 after d, 0.53 after o/r). These are minor descriptive details.
